title: Missing Brute Force Protection / Rate Limiting on Login Endpoint
description: The /api/login.php endpoint does not implement any rate limiting or account lockout mechanisms to prevent brute force attacks. An attacker can send unlimited login attempts with different passwords without any throttling, delays, or account lockouts. The endpoint accepts rapid-fire requests and responds with the same generic error message for all failed attempts, allowing attackers to efficiently brute force credentials. Testing shows 20 consecutive failed login attempts are all accepted without any rate limiting response.
impact: Attackers can perform unlimited brute force attacks against any user account to guess credentials. Combined with the timing-based account enumeration vulnerability, an attacker could identify valid usernames and then brute force their passwords without any restrictions. This makes weak or common passwords extremely vulnerable to compromise. The lack of rate limiting also makes the system vulnerable to dictionary attacks and credential stuffing attacks where attackers try common password combinations. Admin accounts are particularly at risk.
evidence:
POC executed successfully confirming vulnerability:
- All 20 consecutive failed login attempts returned HTTP 200
- Response: {"success":false,"message":"Invalid username or password."}
- No 429 (Too Many Requests) status code
- No 403 (Forbidden) status code
- No rate limiting headers in response
- No account lockout observed
- All attempts accepted without delay or rejection

POC Output:
Total attempts sent: 20
Successful responses (HTTP 200): 20
Rate limit responses (HTTP 429/403): 0
[!] VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: No rate limiting detected!
[!] All 20 attempts were accepted without throttling
references: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Rendered UI Layers or Frames, CWE-799: Improper Control of Interaction Frequency, OWASP - Credential Stuffing, OWASP - Brute Force Attack
toolCallDescription: Document missing rate limiting vulnerability on login endpoint with confirmed POC
